cards.details: Sakas forced out of Central Asia by the Yuezhi, crossing the Hindu Kush into Drangiana (Sakastan).
Maues establishes the first major Saka kingdom in Gandhara and Punjab.
Nahapana of the Western Kshatrapas gains prominence in the Deccan, later defeated by Gautamiputra Satakarni.
Rudradaman I, the most famous Western Kshatrapa, issues the Junagadh Rock Inscription.

items.title: S.K.R.M.
items.decryption: S for System (Kshatrapa), K for Kshatrapa (title), R for Rudradaman (Greatest), M for Maues (Founder).

items: Do not confuse Sakas with Kushanas. Sakas (Indo-Scythians) preceded the main Kushana consolidation.
The Junagadh inscription is the first Sanskrit inscription, not Prakrit, which is a common UPSC trap.
Sakas did not destroy the Mauryan empire; they filled the power vacuum in the Northwest post-Mauryan decline.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Centered in Sakastan (Drangiana).
  • Expanded to Taxila, Mathura, and Ujjain.
  • Western Kshatrapas controlled Gujarat/Kathiawar.

Personalities

  • Maues: First powerful king.
  • Nahapana: Rival to Satavahanas.
  • Rudradaman I: Sanskrit patronage.

Saka Sociopolitical Mindmap

  • Political Structure
    • Kshatrapa System: Governors appointed as 'Kshatrapas' (Satrap) and 'Mahakshatrapas'.
    • Integration: Adopted Indian titles, coinage, and religious practices (Shaivism/Buddhism).
  • The Junagadh Inscription (Rudradaman I)
    • First major epigraphic record in pure Sanskrit.
    • Details the restoration of the Sudarshana Lake (originally built by Chandragupta Maurya).
FeatureSaka Impact
CurrencyHigh-quality silver coinage; standard for trade.
EpigraphyIntroduction of Sanskrit as a formal administrative language.
